newsitem.title: USA: MCA buys talk show syndicator.
newsitem.headline: MCA buys talk show syndicator.

text.p: MCA Inc. said its Television Group agreed Monday to acquire substantially all the assets of talk show syndicator Multimedia Entertainment, the force behind such popular shows as "Sally Jessy Raphael" and "Jerry Springer," from Gannett Co. Inc.
The terms of the deal were not disclosed, but industry sources said Los Angeles-based MCA paid less than $50 million.

MCA is 80 percent owned by Canadian beverage firm Seagram Co. Ltd. of Montreal. Gannett is a major newspaper chain and publishes USA Today. It also operates 15 television stations, 11 radio stations and cable television systems.
The entertainment company also said that Sally Jessy Raphael, host of the longest-running talk show in syndication, had agreed to extend her contract beyond the year 2000.
"As recent multiyear renewals indicate, stations recognise the strength of both 'Sally' and 'Jerry,'" MCA Television Group Chairman Greg Meidel said in a statement.

"Sally Jessy Raphael," which began airing in 1982 and is the No. 2 U.S. talk show, appears in 147 markets covering 92 percent of the United States. "Jerry Springer" appears in 113 markets with 82 percent coverage and is ranked ninth nationally among all talk shows.
Other Multimedia Entertainment talk shows include the recently unveiled "Pat Bullard" show and "Crook & Chase."
Seagram stock rose 5 cents Canadian (4 cents) to C$54.05 ($40.31) in afternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Gannett rose 37.5 cents to $77.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
